greeting.text: Well met. The forge is hot if you need steel.

warn.text: Bandits camp east of the mill. Kestrel keeps them off us — buys his blades from me, so I've a stake in him coming home.

kin.text: Elowen the trader's my sister. She keeps the coin, I keep the coal. We do well enough between us.

grieve_elowen.text: My sister. The shop's shuttered and the forge feels twice as cold. Whoever did it had best pray the guard finds them before I do.

mourn.text: We've buried one of our own lately. If you've a strong arm, the road east could use watching.

inventory.name: Bread
inventory.description: A heel of bread. Restores a little health.

greeting.text: Coin for potions, potions for coin. What'll it be?

responses.text: Where do your goods come from?
You mentioned a task… (The Lost Amulet)

supply.text: Bram's farm keeps my shelves stocked — bread, flax, what have you. My brother Thalen forges the rest into something worth selling.

grieve_thalen.text: My brother, gone. He was all bluster and hammer, but he was mine. Don't expect me to smile today.

offer_lost_amulet.text: Elowen lost her grandmother's amulet somewhere in the woods.

handin_lost_amulet.text: Oh! Oh, it's warm still — just like she said. Thank you. Please, take these.

inventory.name: Pitchfork

greeting.text: Long day in the fields. The crop's good this year, thank the gods.

mara.text: Mara? Down at the square, most days. She fancies the guard, Kestrel — thinks I don't notice. Good lad, though. I'll allow it.

grieve_mara.text: My little sister. I keep looking up expecting her to come down the lane. The fields can rot for all I care today.

greeting.text: Move along, citizen. I've bandits to watch for.

responses.text: Anyone you're watching over in particular?

mara.text: The whole town. But... Mara, if you're asking. Don't you dare let anything happen to her while I'm out on the wall.

grieve_mara.text: Say her name again and I'll not answer for what I do. I'll cut down every last bandit east of the mill, or die trying.

greeting.text: Spare a coin? A man's got to eat...

gossip.text: Me? I hear everything. Owe old Thalen three silver, mind — don't tell him you saw me. And that guard's sweet on Mara, if you didn't know.

gossip_mourn.text: Aye. A death in a place this small, everyone feels it. Even a beggar bows his head. Coin doesn't warm you the same after.

greeting.text: Millbrook's a quiet place, mostly. We like it that way.

responses.text: Kestrel fell defending the town. I'm sorry.
You mentioned a task… (A Word with Wick)

folk.text: My brother Bram works the east fields. And Kestrel keeps the square — he pretends it's duty, but he lingers by me longer than the others.

grieve_kestrel.text: He said he'd always come home from the wall. He lied. I don't know how to be here without him watching the square.

grieve_bram.text: My brother. The farm's just dirt now, without him cursing at the crows. I've no one left but the memory of him.

offer_a_word_with_wick.text: Mara frets that old Wick hasn't been seen today. Would you look in on him?

greeting.text: Fresh from the mere, or near enough. Mind the mudcrabs, they bite.

fish.text: Poor, since the smugglers came. They work nights, boats with no lanterns. Osric's seen them.

handin_mirrormere_smugglers.text: Ha! The lake is ours again. Here — you've earned every coin.

offer_mirrormere_smugglers.text: Smugglers have made a nest of the south shore — they cut my nets and sell my catch back to me in Hollin's Cross. Scout the cove and put them to flight.

greeting.text: The ferry doesn't run. Not while those cutthroats sit on the south shore.

cove.text: Past the far bank, due south-west. They beached a proper ship there, stolen I'd wager.

strange.text: Fires on the old hill north of the village some nights. Barrow Hill. Nobody goes up there any more.

greeting.text: Hrm. You've the look of someone who's never been hit properly.

guild.text: We fight what the watch won't. Wolves, wights, greenskins. Coin's fair and the ale's free.

handin_fighters_join.text: Six? More, by the look of your shield. Welcome to the Guild.

offer_fighters_join.text: The Guild doesn't take talkers. Skeletons walk on Barrow Hill, north of Millbrook. Put six of them back in the ground and you're one of us.

greeting.text: Welcome to the Tipsy Hollin! Bed's ten coin, ale's two, gossip's free.

gossip.text: Ysolde's been asking for someone to clear the spiders out of Webwood, down the south road. And Brother Ansel won't shut up about cultists east of here.

greeting.text: Don't mind me. Third ale. Or fourth.

see.text: There's a witch on the knoll way up north-east. Mother Nettle. Makes a potion that'll cure anything but a hangover.

inventory.description: Slow, but it caves in armour.
inventory.name: Iron Warhammer

greeting.text: Steel, sharp and honest. No refunds if you cut yourself.

handin_silk_and_venom.text: Good. Now I can send for silk without burying a courier. Take this bow — it'll serve you better than mine did me.

offer_silk_and_venom.text: Webwood, down the south road — the spiders have grown bold, and one of them's the size of a cart. Kill six and bring me word. I'll make it worth your while.

greeting.text: Leather for the quick, iron for the stubborn. Which are you?

armour.text: Depends if you'd rather dodge a bear or stand there and let it chew. I'd dodge.

greeting.text: I keep the peace, the books and the tolls at Hollin's Cross. Mostly the tolls.

responses.text: Any work going? (Trouble at the Old Mill)

cross.text: Four roads meet here: Millbrook west, the downs south, the cultist wastes east, and trouble in every direction.

handin_mill_bandits.text: Then the carts can roll again. The Cross thanks you — and so does my purse, reluctantly.

offer_mill_bandits.text: Bandits hold the old mill north-east of Millbrook — the grain for three villages sits under their boots. Clear them out and the Cross will pay you well.

greeting.text: Peace upon you, traveller. Though peace is thin on the ground this year.

cult.text: They call themselves the Ashen Circle. They believe the vale must burn to be reborn. I believe they are simply mad.

handin_ashen_circle.text: Then there will be one less fire in the world tonight. Take these wards — and my blessing, for what it weighs.

offer_ashen_circle.text: East of here, past the last milestone, men in grey robes burn things that should not burn. Find their circle, and end it. The gods will not; they have asked me to ask you.

greeting.text: Keep your blade sheathed inside the Cross and we'll get along.

responses.text: Any work going? (Greenskins at the Gate)

quiet.text: Never. Wolves in Greywood, smugglers on the mere, and now greenskins to the east.

handin_greenskin_warcamp.text: You did what my whole watch couldn't. Take this, and the Cross's thanks.

offer_greenskin_warcamp.text: Greenskins have dug in east along the road — a proper warcamp, palisade and all. My watch is three men and a dog. Thin their numbers before they come for the Cross.

greeting.text: Eyes on the road, citizen.

greeting.text: Oakridge Farm. We feed Millbrook, the Cross, and every boar in Greywood.

responses.text: The boars won't trouble your fields.
Any work going? (Blight in the Barley)

handin_blight_in_the_barley.text: Bless you. Take this — and there's always a heel of bread here for you.

offer_blight_in_the_barley.text: Wild boar out of Greywood, rooting up half my carrots every night. Kill four of the brutes and I'll see you fed and paid.

greeting.text: If you're after work, Hobb's the one to ask. I just dig.

road.text: Wherever the coin is. Hollin's Cross for the markets, the farm for bread, and never Greywood after dark. Wolves.

inventory.description: A rough grey pelt worth a few coins.

greeting.text: Walk soft in Greywood. Every wolf in the vale seems to have moved in.

responses.text: Any work going? (The Beast of Frostcap)

camp.text: Deeper in, west, there's a camp nobody came back to. Pretty trinket in the dirt there, I saw — not mine to take.

handin_frostcap_yeti.text: You actually did it! I owe you more than coin — take my best bow and fletching.

offer_frostcap_yeti.text: Far north-east, past Nettle's knoll, Frostcap Tor. There's a white beast on the summit that's killed two of my dogs and a trapper. I'm too old for the climb. Kill it.

greeting.text: Easy, easy. You'll spook the flock.

responses.text: Any work going? (A Culling of Wolves)

sheep.text: Best fleece in the vale. Hobb at Oakridge will tell you otherwise. Hobb is wrong.

handin_wolves.text: The flock'll sleep easy — and so will I. The bow's yours.

offer_wolves.text: Wolves take a ewe a night off my flock. They den up north, in the rocks past the field. Kill five of them and I'll give you my old hunting bow.

inventory.description: Silvered steel; bites deep into the undead.
inventory.name: Silver Sword

inventory.description: A staff that channels a bolt of flame.
inventory.name: Apprentice's Staff

inventory.description: Grants 20 points of shield for 30 seconds.

inventory.description: A staff that channels a bolt of flame.
inventory.name: Apprentice's Staff

greeting.text: Come in, come in. Don't touch the jars, they touch back.

witch.text: I'm an old woman who knows which leaves kill you. In this vale that makes me a witch.

handin_nettle_nightshade.text: Lovely, deadly things. Here, dearie: something to keep you breathing.

offer_nettle_nightshade.text: My shelves want nightshade — five blooms. It grows on these slopes and along the old road south, where the shroomlings creep. Mind them; they bite.

greeting.text: Pots mended, blades sharpened, questions answered for a copper. Greenskins east, mind. I don't go further than this milestone.
Walked from the coast to see Frostcap. My knees regret it.

see.text: Hollin's Cross, south past Millbrook — good ale. Mirrormere at sunset. Don't go near the hill with the stones on it.
